children: Director of National Intelligence
Jay Clayton
has reportedly been appointed to serve as the
Trump
administration’s AI czar and will lead a new White House “Super Intelligence Force.”

According to Clayton, a new White House task force will have 120 days to report on the risks and opportunities of AI and determine the federal government’s responsibility, The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday.

“The president asked that a group be put together that was going to ensure exactly what he said,” Clayton said, that “we stay the leaders in superintelligence, and that the interests of the American people are put first.”

Clayton was confirmed in July to lead the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. He previously served as the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York and later headed the Securities and Exchange Commission during the first Trump administration.
Trump Signaled Support, Sought Input First
The move follows an earlier WSJ report that President
Donald Trump
was expected to name Clayton to the role.

The new “Super Intelligence Force” will examine the risks and opportunities posed by AI and recommend what role the federal government should play in overseeing the technology. Speaking on CNBC, Clayton said the work would be an extension of his current role, given the growing security threats posed by AI.
“This is very much a part of I would say the same portfolio, which is protecting the American people,” he said.
